item.title: Vendor failed to meet contractual obligations: Foxconn on payment dispute
item.description: Taiwanese electronics giant Foxconn on Wednesday alleged that a certain vendor in India has failed to meet agreed contractual obligations. BCD Emprassa, a vendor of Hon Hai Technology Group (Foxconn), has reportedly moved the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) to recover alleged dues of around USD 15 million from the company. "Foxconn clarifies that the dispute arises from the supplier's failure to meet agreed contractual requirements and quality standards. Despite repeated requests for corrective action, the outstanding issues remain unresolved," the company said. BCD Emprassa has reportedly filed a claim regarding 700 residential units for female employees working at its Bengaluru facility. Foxconn said that as the matter is now subject to legal proceedings, the company will take appropriate steps to safeguard its legitimate rights and interests through the legal process and will refrain from commenting further on the specifics of the case. item.title: Amazon's India exports cross $27 billion, exporter base grows 20%
item.description: E-commerce major Amazon on Wednesday said it has reached USD 27 billion in cumulative exports from India through its Amazon Global Selling programme, with the number of exporters on the platform rising 20 per cent in a year to 2.4 lakh. The milestone marks progress towards Amazon's goal of enabling USD 80 billion in cumulative e-commerce exports from India by 2030, the company said in a statement. Launched in 2015, the programme has enabled the sale of more than one billion 'Made-in-India' products to customers across Amazon's global marketplaces. Delhi, with over 36,000 exporters, tops the list of states and Union Territories on the programme, followed by Rajasthan (over 32,500), Uttar Pradesh (over 29,000), Gujarat (over 28,000) and Maharashtra (over 23,500), according to the company.
